newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil rethinks debt maturity policy - paper.
newsitem.headline: Brazil rethinks debt maturity policy - paper.

text.p: Expectations of a sharper drop in interest rates in coming months may cause Brazil's National Treasury to slow down the rate at which it is lengthening the average maturity of its debt, a local newspaper said.
Gazeta Mercantil, citing no source, said the Central Bank and the Treasury combined have some 127.3 billion reais in debt circulating in the marketplace, 70 percent of it expiring in March.

In August, the Treasury began issuing pre-fixed 12-month debt securities in an attempt to roll over some of its debt. But the paper said the Treasury still preferred to issue nine-month debt to avoid the risk of getting locked in at a higher interest rate on its longer-term paper.
The newspaper said monthly interest rates have fallen from roughly four percent at the start of 1995 to about 1.8 percent today but internal debt has tripled in that time.
